drawer.confidenceHelp: Fist to five: instead of a metric you enter a level from 1 to 5 — “{low}” to “{high}”. Scale and target are fixed; below 3 the goal is replanned. For goals that no single number can measure.
drawer.freiesLabelDerMessgroesse: Free-text label for the measure, e.g. customers or units. With metric type Custom it is appended as a suffix to every displayed value.
drawer.gewichtImRollupDes: Weight in the parent goal's rollup (empty = 1)
drawer.wieStarkDiesesUnterziel: How much this sub-goal counts in the parent goal's average. Empty = 1 (all sub-goals weighted equally).
drawer.verantwortlichFuerDiesesZiel: Accountable for this goal. From the tenant's users.
drawer.worausSichDerFortschritt: How progress is calculated: Manual (you maintain the value yourself), From sub-goals (average of the children), KPI tree (leaf: actuals from linked epic KPIs; branch: sub-goal values cascade up, measured by value) or Confidence vote (fist to five instead of a metric).
drawer.zaehltNichtImAutomatischen: Excluded from this goal's automatic progress
drawer.kpiTreeBranch: KPI tree as a branch: the sub-goals' values cascade upward, and attainment is measured by value (value reached ÷ target) rather than as an average of the sub-goals. Each sub-goal needs its conversion factor into this unit — without it, it contributes nothing.
drawer.kpiTreeLeaf: KPI tree as a leaf: the actual comes from the linked epic KPIs (Δ × factor). Without a link the goal stays at 0%.
drawer.kpiTreeLeafNoPortfolio: KPI tree as a leaf draws its actual from linked epic KPIs — and the portfolio module is not enabled here. With sub-goals the mode works without it: their values cascade up and attainment is measured by value.
drawer.rollupHelp: Progress = weighted average of the sub-goals. A metric of its own is ignored.
drawer.kpiLinkHelp: The KPIs of linked epics form this goal's actual value via Δ × conversion factor (progress source “KPI tree”).

rtb.wasDieserWertstromLaufend: What this value stream needs on an ongoing basis appears here — once the first item exists.
rtb.mitArtZaehltDie: With an ART the item counts directly against it. Without an ART and without a solution it is spread evenly across all ARTs of the value stream.
